subject: Problem with building SNP map for sex chromosomes

messages.author: f67c068826461884
messages.subject: Problem with building SNP map for sex chromosomes
parts:
Dear all,

We are building a linkage map with SNP data for a mammal - classic XY system of sex determination.

Data structure: >1600 individuals (all males), thousands of markers, advanced intercross population (Fn).

We have been able to build maps for all autosomes, however, we have not been able to get a map fo the X chromosome. 

We did include "Sex" as a phenotype in the data file and coded all males as 1.

It looks like all X-linked markers are being excluded because of this filter, as we only have AA and BB genotypes in the dataset (all males):

#### Filter of frequency (1:2:1)
gt <- geno.table(mapthis)
gt[gt$P.value < 0.05/totmar(mapthis),]
todrop <- rownames(gt[gt$P.value < 1e-10,])
tokeep <- rownames(gt[gt$P.value >= 1e-10,])

Any pointers on how to keep the X-linked markers and get them mapped will be greatly appreciated.

Cheers,

Patricia

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Problem with building SNP map for sex chromosomes
parts:
I think just don’t use that filter. Only omit markers that you think are bad.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Problem with building SNP map for sex chromosomes
parts:
When looking at the genotype frequencies at markers, we’re trying to distinguish between “real” biologic deviation from Mendel’s rules, where it should be that all of the markers on a chromosome are deviating in the same way. If you see that, all is fine. I’d say a marker looks bad if it’s behaving quite differently from those around it. 

But if you don’t know the order of markers, it can be hard to tell between these cases. Requires a bit of trial and error.

karl
